terms.title: Cellulose acetate
terms.tooltip: The plastic filter material most cigarette filters are made from.
terms.explanation: Cellulose acetate is the thermoplastic material in the filter of a finished cigarette. Recovering it intact is the goal of the solvent-based routes; the washing and incorporation routes keep it physically intact but chemically unchanged. Its properties after any recycling route are not established for the material collected from cigarette filters, because no located source characterises the recovered polymer on a comparable basis.

terms.title: Nicotine
terms.tooltip: The main soluble residue carried by the tobacco and the filter.
terms.explanation: Nicotine is the best-studied contaminant of cigarette butts because it is soluble in water and is the residue most consistently described as being partly leached by washing. No located source reports nicotine removal efficiency for any recycling route on a stated mass basis, so the fraction removed remains unknown rather than small.

terms.title: Tobacco-specific nitrosamines
terms.tooltip: Carcinogenic compounds formed during tobacco combustion.
terms.explanation: Tobacco-specific nitrosamines, of which NNN and NNK are the ones most often named, are part of the combustion residue carried by butts. They are named here because any credible measurement of contaminant fate has to include them; no located source reports their partitioning across any recycling route.

terms.title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
terms.tooltip: Combustion-derived compounds that many routes redistribute rather than remove.
terms.explanation: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are the combustion residue most often described as being only partly transferred to the wash liquor. Because several routes simply encapsulate the butt material rather than treating it, the question for them is not removal but whether the compound can later escape the product.

terms.title: Heavy metals
terms.tooltip: Cadmium, lead, arsenic and mercury, treated as a stop condition rather than a parameter.
terms.explanation: Heavy metals are treated throughout this layer as a stop condition rather than as a value to be averaged or traded off. A stream whose heavy-metal content has not been characterised cannot be routed to a product or to unclassified waste, and a favourable result on another criterion does not offset that.

terms.title: Tar and combustion residues
terms.tooltip: The sticky combustion residue that binds other residues to the butt.
terms.explanation: Tar and associated combustion residues are the fraction that makes washing difficult: they are only partly soluble in water and partly soluble in organic solvents, so no simple sequence of washes removes them completely. No located source quantifies what remains after any route.

terms.title: Microplastics
terms.tooltip: Small plastic fragments produced when filters are handled or degraded.
terms.explanation: The cellulose acetate filter is itself a source of microplastic fragments, and size reduction steps turn butts into a particle stream. Washing does not remove that potential, and partial biological degradation does not eliminate it. The magnitude is not measured in any located source.

terms.title: Dry-mass basis
terms.tooltip: A way of counting mass that does not change with how wet the material is.
terms.explanation: A dry-mass basis states the mass of material excluding water, so that a wet lot and a dried lot of the same material can be compared. Without it, two reported splits can describe the same material, and a balance cannot be checked. Several published figures for this material do not state whether they were measured wet or dry.

terms.title: Analyte-resolved contaminant fate
terms.tooltip: Knowing where each named contaminant ends up, not just that the total is smaller.
terms.explanation: Analyte-resolved contaminant fate means that for each named contaminant, the mass in each output stream is reported so that the mass leaving the process can be compared with the mass entering it. A total contaminant number cannot do this job, and a single favourable removal figure for one analyte does not transfer to another.

terms.title: The four-field sink
terms.tooltip: The four things that must be located before a recovered material can be called a product.
terms.explanation: The four fields are a dry-mass balance on a common dry-feed basis, analyte-resolved contaminant fate across the streams, a named final treatment route with a jurisdiction-specific acceptance basis, and a use-specific product gate that is independent of whether the mass balance closes. A method family that cannot locate all four is a hypothesis with a measurement plan attached, not a finished route.

material.title: Cigarette butt
material.description: The filter, the paper, the remaining tobacco and the ash left in a finished cigarette after it has been smoked, as collected from ash trays, bins and street litter.
material.compositionSummary: A spent cigarette butt is a layered composite rather than a single material: a cellulose acetate filter tow, a paper wrapper carrying combustion residue, a short tobacco rod that retains tobacco-specific compounds, and fine ash. What matters for every recycling route is that these layers carry different contaminants, so a process that treats the butt as one material will either leave some contaminants untouched or redistribute them without removing them.

hypotheses.title: Separate the filter before washing
hypotheses.visibleLabel: AI hypothesis: separating the filter-rich fraction first may change where the contamination goes.
hypotheses.priorContext: Mechanical separation and staged washing are already described in the literature and patents. Fibre-release tests and pulping liquor data flag two potential losses that bulk recovered mass alone would miss. This candidate combines existing ideas for comparison, not as a claim of novelty.
hypotheses.mechanism: Compare early separation followed by contained staged washing with washing without early separation. Account for the separated tobacco and paper, fibres or solids captured from the wash, dissolved wash residues, and the recovered filter material. Keep the recovered material on hold until independent intended-use evidence is available.
assumptions: Some contamination may follow the rejected fraction rather than the recovered filter. The direction and size of that split are unknown for individual contaminants.
Early separation may lose useful filter fibre. Comparing contaminant load per unit of recovered filter matters alongside total waste-stream loads.
The two routes would be compared using comparable feed, the same measurement basis and a defined non-contact end use.
unresolvedDependencies: Measured partition by contaminant, including cadmium, lead, arsenic and mercury.
Fibre loss, occupational exposure, wash residues, treatment acceptance and independent end-use measurements.
failureModes: The lower wash load comes at the expense of unmanageable solid rejects.
Fibre losses or weak separation leave equal or greater contaminant load per unit of recovered filter.
falsifiers: Comparable runs show no meaningful reduction in the wash load at an agreed fibre recovery, or show greater residual load per recovered fibre for the contaminant being evaluated.
The mass balance cannot account for the lost contaminant, a metals stream remains uncharacterised, or an output lacks a documented receiving route.

hypotheses.title: Batch-02 Invention Sketch: Four-Field Sink as Mandatory Pilot Prerequisite
hypotheses.visibleLabel: Four-field sink accounting as a stop-condition prerequisite for any authorized pilot
hypotheses.priorContext: Batch-01 identified cigarette butt recycling as an open problem with no located evidence of full-butt recycling at any scale. Six method families were catalogued (mechanical-physical, thermal, chemical, biological, material-incorporation, product-routes). Batch-01 established heavy metals as an explicit stop condition. Batch-02 reviewed all six families and found each fails at least one field of the four-field sink: dry-mass closure, analyte-resolved contaminant fate, use-specific product gate, and metals stop condition. No family demonstrates a complete dry-mass balance with analyte-resolved accounting; no family shows where each measured analyte goes through every process step; no family sets an independent product-quality gate separate from mass-balance closure; no family treats metals as an explicit stop condition with a demonstrated analytical test.
hypotheses.mechanism: This hypothesis proposes that the four-field sink (dry-mass balance on a common dry-feed basis, analyte-resolved contaminant fate across all output streams, a named final treatment route with a jurisdiction-specific acceptance basis, and a use-specific product gate independent of mass-balance closure) must be a mandatory prerequisite for any later authorized pilot. The metals stop-condition is in force: any detectable metal above background in feedstock, wash water, air emission, solid residue, or final product triggers a halt; the stream cannot resume until analytical performance (inlet-to-outlet) is demonstrated. This sketch does not propose how to remove metals; it proposes that metals are a stop condition, not a solvable parameter within this sketch. The six method families remain as unvalidated inputs to this prerequisite framework.
assumptions: The six method families are a working grouping of the routes reviewed here, not an exhaustive inventory of known approaches.
Heavy metals (cadmium, lead, arsenic, mercury) are correctly treated as a stop condition rather than a parameter to be traded off.
A mass balance that is not dry-mass-based and analyte-resolved cannot establish that contaminants have been removed rather than redistributed.
A product gate that depends on mass-balance closure is circular and does not protect the intended use.
The sources used in the original sketch did not establish complete inlet-to-outlet accounting across all relevant streams.
unresolvedDependencies: Quantitative input-output data at pilot scale for any of the six method families.
Demonstrated analytical method performance for heavy metals across all process streams (inlet-to-outlet).
A use-specific product-quality standard for any recovered material from cigarette butts.
Novelty/patentability search — this sketch has NOT performed one.
Regulatory acceptance basis for any final route in any jurisdiction.
failureModes: A later pilot demonstrates that one or more method families can achieve dry-mass and analyte-resolved closure without meeting the four-field sink prerequisite, falsifying the necessity claim.
Heavy metals are shown to be consistently below background in all process streams for a family, making the stop condition moot for that family.
A jurisdiction accepts a recovered material based on total contaminant limits rather than analyte-resolved fate, making the analyte-resolved field unnecessary in that context.
A product gate is established that is independent of mass-balance closure and is met by a family without the four-field sink being fully satisfied.
The metals stop-condition cannot be analytically implemented at the required sensitivity, making the prerequisite infeasible.
falsifiers: Published pilot-scale data showing complete dry-mass balance with analyte-resolved contaminant fate for any of the six families.
Published analytical method validation demonstrating inlet-to-outlet performance for cadmium, lead, arsenic, and mercury across all process streams for any family.
A regulatory acceptance decision for a cigarette-butt-derived product that does not require analyte-resolved fate.
A demonstrated product-quality gate that is independent of mass-balance closure and is passed by a family without the four-field sink.

hypotheses.title: Scientist-Inventor Batch-02 Proposals: M01-Gate, J-H-01-M, F3-SC, F2-VSC, F5-ED
hypotheses.visibleLabel: Five falsifiable engineering variants with executable simulations and metals stop-condition guardrails
hypotheses.priorContext: Batch-02 established that all six method families fail at least one field of the four-field sink. The Scientist-Inventor role (operator-authorized 2026-11-17) produced five falsifiable engineering variants (M01-Gate, J-H-01-M, F3-SC, F2-VSC, F5-ED) with executable simulations, each designed to address the metals stop-condition and the four-field sink prerequisite.
hypotheses.mechanism: Each variant pairs an upstream M01-Gate (dry-pneumatic + triboelectric pre-fractionation) with a downstream polishing step (counter-current wash + GAC/IDA, microfiltration + EtOH/CO2 antisolvent, vacuum-vented extrusion + acid/S-GAC, or BMED + CIP) to close the four-field sink: dry-mass balance, analyte-resolved fate, named treatment route, and use-specific product gate.
assumptions: M01-Gate diverts >=75% of Cd, Pb, As mass into the ash/fines + residual tobacco fraction.
GAC/IDA, EtOH/CO2, acid/S-GAC, and BMED polishing reduce residual nicotine/metals below Tier-1/Tier-2 use-gate limits.
All simulations use representative feed loadings and are labeled ai_inference / ai_proposal, not measured values.
unresolvedDependencies: Authorized M01-M08 laboratory measurement to validate partition coefficients and polishing efficiency.
Qualified facility, risk assessment, and lawful contaminated-waste handling for any physical execution.
failureModes: M01-Gate leaves >25% of Cd/Pb/As/Hg on CA tow.
Polishing fails to keep Cycle-20 CA nicotine <50 mg/kg dry or Cd/Pb below use-gate limits.
Membrane/sorbent fouling or solvent recovery failure exceeds cost or energy thresholds.
falsifiers: ICP-MS/OES showing >25% Cd/Pb/As/Hg remaining on CA tow post-M01-Gate.
Cycle-20 CA nicotine >50 mg/kg dry or Cd/Pb exceeding use-gate limits.
BMED current efficiency <85% at Cycle 10 or post-CIP <90%.
